findings.what: Blocking source-model error: EARTHLING_DATA[24] excludes valid category 24. The data inventory explicitly describes a twenty-fifth logical 38-byte record at 0x02638a (37 owned bytes plus its final byte overlapping EarthlingCoordinatePairs), with the hot-tub state/contact definition. LevelEarthlingChoices selects kind 24 at level 0 slot 18, while population/state/display/touch code indexes EARTHLING_DATA by kind, making those accesses outside the declared array. The authors mistook a non-overlapping asset partition for the logical array extent. This is not an original gameplay bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare EARTHLING_DATA[25] consistently in all five files and preserve/document the final padding-byte overlap as appropriate. All five complete alternatives under alternatives/twenty-five-definitions-* independently MATCH both revisions; evidence is additional-alternative-results.json and definition-extent-evidence.json. Reprepare after correcting the bound.

findings.what: Avoidable cross-unit declaration differences remain. The new behavior units declare the char-returning func_0196b0/func_01aa20 as int and call it an ORIGINAL BUG, but correct char declarations together reproduce every consumer, so word result stores do not establish an implicit-int historical declaration. The two new func_015da6 callers declare void although its accepted definition returns short. The new abs consumers use int instead of the existing long convention, and dispatch declares the shared P1_MENU_OPEN array as a scalar. No emitted-byte necessity was found for these choices.
findings.suggested_fix: Use extern char for both decision helpers in all three consumers and remove their unsupported ORIGINAL BUG claims; use extern short func_015da6 in dispatch and movement_decision; use long abs in the two new consumers; use the P1_MENU_OPEN array view with [0] at the dispatch test. Every alternative MATCHes both revisions, including both helper declarations together in generic, animation and behavior. Retain the separately packet-backed allocator/terrain qualifications. Historical caller declarations remain [INFERENCE].

findings.what: Physical offsets agree, but the same earthling_state tag denotes different six-, sixteen- and eighteen-byte member sets; the same-tag earthling_definition declarations also differ across external EARTHLING_DATA consumers. Partial consumers currently avoid using the wrong record stride, so no current byte mismatch was found, but this is not one consistent cross-unit C record. Matching common declarations are available.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse a complete shared 18-byte earthling_state and 38-byte earthling_definition, preserving per-kind health/phase reuse and existing neutral two-byte trailing storage where needed. The five common-eighteen-byte-record wave-18 alternatives match both revisions and agree with the three existing wave-17 layouts; all five common-thirty-eight-byte-definition alternatives also match. Prefer normal shared-header consolidation over additional incompatible local views. Do not use the initial scalarized-tail experiment that failed LoadInEarthlings.

findings.what: The ownership comment calls 0x019c96 the common tail. It is the third switch-table target, sets negative horizontal velocity, and branches to 0x019ca4, the actual join. The catalogue merge itself is correct.
